analysis:
All four changed files are documentation or changelog text only: two changelog.d fragments, docs/developer/build.md (new paragraph at head lines 27-31) and docs/developer/test.md (new 'Provider authorization guidance' section). No source code, protocol, key-handling or policy logic is in this batch, so I could not verify the described status/doctor/unenroll behavior.

The documented behavior is consistent with TB-011/T-053/T-057. Status and doctor will keep showing App Attest authorization until the coordinator lease expires, instead of requiring a renewal within 10 seconds. MDM removal guidance requires a fresh coordinator decision, which matches the TB-011 text on ReceiptDecisionFreshness and 'fresh current coordinator decision'. `darkbloom unenroll` checks are stated as unchanged, so the destructive action keeps its stricter gate. The status display is not a serving or trust authority per TB-011 ('badges/diagnostics grant no permission'), and the change makes removal advice more conservative, not less.

The test docs claim ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests uses fixed snapshots and does not run host probes, change profiles or claim native Apple acceptance. That is a reasonable non-overclaiming statement (T-056). I found no new attack surface and no assumption invalidated by the docs.

Remaining integration questions: the Swift implementation that backs these docs (status, doctor, shared readiness helper) is not in the supplied batch. Whether lease-expiry display could be confused with removal readiness, and whether the 'unexpired lease' check uses the coordinator-supplied expiry rather than a local clock, is unverified from this evidence and should be examined if the code changes appear in another batch.
